Batch: JoeWare AccExp, ATSN and Auth publisher source review and acquisition retry

Findings: Auth 01.01.00 dated 2001-08-17; publisher MD5 3758b8df84e839c870be1923f790bb99 and SHA-1 a6d1a2a560c74f39145a81be4918890af028b7ff.
Sources.DigestBoundary: Publisher MD5/SHA-1 are source-list observations, not locally verified archive hashes.

Sources.Finding: Publisher identifies AccExp as a command-line account-expiration reader/modifier; minimum account-operator rights are listed for domain targets and administrator rights for member/standalone targets. Historical platform list ends at Windows XP.
Usage distinguishes account expiration from password expiration and supports viewing, setting a date, or setting expiration to NEVER; it may target a named machine.
Publisher identifies ATSN as an Active Directory query that maps IP addresses to site/subnet and lists Windows 2000, Server 2003 and XP.
ATSN accepts IPs or an input file, can target a chosen domain controller, and can write results to an output file. No target was contacted.
Publisher identifies Auth as a credential authentication test, lists Windows NT, 2000, Server 2003 and XP, and notes SE_TCB_NAME is required on Windows 2000 or earlier.

AcquisitionAttempt.Result: Failed before the source version list was fetched because local DNS could not resolve the JoeWare publisher host.

Resolved: Current publisher version rows and product-purpose/usage details for AccExp, ATSN and Auth.
Deferred: Exact ZIP bytes, local SHA-256 and member inventories.
Isolated synthetic account-expiration, directory lookup and credential-test acceptance.
Windows 11 support; the publisher platform claims are historical.

Estimate.Adjustment: Unchanged; source review and a pre-transfer DNS failure do not establish package bytes, lifecycle or functional acceptance.
